around.headline: Drones deployed in search for Bengaluru techie missing on Shivagange trek
around.summary: Search teams have brought in drones to widen the hunt for the 31-year-old IT professional who went missing while trekking alone at Shivagange over the weekend; he was due to be married in a few months. If you're heading out on a solo trek, share your live location and planned return time with someone before you set off.

around.headline: CCB busts racket making rigged gambling cards, one held in R.T. Nagar
around.summary: Bengaluru's Central Crime Branch arrested a man running an operation that manufactured marked or 'rigged' playing cards used to fix card games and gambling dens. Card games with strangers for money are a common setup for this kind of fraud — assume any deck offered by the house could be tampered with.

around.summary: Local roundups are flagging a bandh call for August 13, alongside this week's food-safety raids and detentions. Details of the bandh's organisers and scope weren't in today's reports, but it's worth checking for transport and shop-closure updates before you plan travel that day.

around.headline: Bengaluru metro pillar collapse: 8 officials named in FIR
around.summary: Police have named eight officials in the FIR over the earlier metro pillar collapse and sent notices to the contractors involved, a step toward accountability for the incident. If your commute runs past active metro construction, keep giving barricaded and under-construction stretches a wide berth.

around.headline: Bengaluru ranked India's most congested city in new TomTom report
around.summary: A fresh TomTom traffic index places Bengaluru at the top of India's congestion rankings. Nothing new for regular commuters, but it's a good prompt to build extra buffer time into evening travel plans, especially with rain in the forecast tonight.

around.headline: Assam flood death toll rises to 100, over 1.3 lakh affected
around.summary: The flood situation in Assam has worsened, with the death toll climbing to around 100 and more than 1.3 lakh people affected across the state. It's a reminder to check in on any friends or family in the Northeast, and a good moment to consider donating to verified relief efforts if you're able to.

street_smart.title: You're selling an old phone to a stranger who came through an online listing. They pay by UPI, immediately show you a 'payment successful' screenshot on their phone, and say they're in a hurry. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No single Bengaluru incident in today's feeds fit this format cleanly, so this rotates in from the evergreen list: UPI fraud and fake payment screenshots, a scam that plays out constantly around resale and delivery handoffs.
street_smart.situation: A buyer has come to collect an item you listed online. They tap out a payment on their phone, turn the screen to show you a green 'Payment Successful' message, and start edging toward the door saying they're late for something.

choices.text: Hand over the item once you've seen the success screenshot on their phone.
choices.feedback: A screenshot proves nothing — it can be doctored in seconds with a screenshot editor, or it can be a real 'payment initiated' screen for a transfer that later fails or gets reversed. The only proof that matters is money actually landing in your account, which you haven't checked yet.

choices.text: Open your own bank or UPI app and wait for the credit (or the SMS/app notification) to show up before handing over the item.
choices.feedback: Correct. Checking your own account is the only way to confirm the money actually moved — a buyer's screen, no matter how convincing, is not evidence of anything on your end. Real payments show up within seconds; if it doesn't, don't hand over the item.

choices.text: Ask them to also send a screenshot of their bank statement showing the debit, then let them go.
choices.feedback: This is just as fakeable as the first screenshot and doesn't replace checking your own account — a debit screenshot from their side tells you nothing about whether you actually received it.

choices.text: Let them leave, planning to check your balance in a few minutes since UPI transfers are usually instant anyway.
choices.feedback: Transfers usually are instant, which is exactly why there's no reason to let the buyer leave before you've confirmed it — if the payment never arrives, they and the item are both gone by the time you check.

takeaways: Never release goods or cash based on a screenshot alone — always confirm the credit in your own bank/UPI app or via the actual SMS/notification before the other person leaves.
Genuine UPI transfers land within seconds; if a 'successful' payment hasn't shown up in your account yet, treat that as a red flag, not a delay.

If you do get scammed, note the buyer's UPI ID and phone number immediately and report it via the National Cybercrime Helpline (1930) or cybercrime.gov.in — fast reporting improves the odds of freezing the funds.

quiz.question: What technology have search teams deployed to help locate a Bengaluru techie missing since the weekend on a solo trek?
quiz.why: Shivagange, where the techie went missing, is a popular monsoon trekking spot near Bengaluru but has steep, exposed terrain that turns treacherous in wet weather.

quiz.question: A new TomTom traffic index report ranks Bengaluru as India's _____ city.
quiz.why: Bengaluru has topped or near-topped global and national congestion indices for several years running, driven by rapid vehicle growth outpacing road and public transit capacity.

quiz.question: The death toll from flooding in Assam has risen to around how many, per the latest reports?
quiz.why: Over 1.3 lakh people have been affected across the state as the flood situation continues to worsen this monsoon season.

quiz.question: Which institution sets India's repo rate, the key interest rate that influences loan and EMI costs?
quiz.why: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee reviews and sets the repo rate roughly every two months, and changes to it typically feed through to home and vehicle loan interest rates with a lag.

quiz.question: What is the longest river in India?
quiz.why: The Ganga runs roughly 2,525 km from its source at Gangotri in the Himalayas to the Bay of Bengal, and its basin supports about a third of India's population.
